title: A list in an array
summary: Inserting in the middle of an array means shifting everything after it. Compare that with a linked list.

checkpoints.text: The list keeps its values in an array of 8 cells and counts how many are in use: 4. The rest of the array is spare room.
To make room for 30 at position 2, the values after it move one cell right, starting from the end: 50 is copied into cell 4 first.
Then 40 moves into cell 3. Cell 2 is free to be overwritten.
30 goes into cell 2. Two values had to move; inserting at the front would move all of them, so insertion is O(n).
Removing the first value: everything after it moves one cell left to close the gap.
20 30 40 50. Reading items[k] is instant (O(1)), which a linked list cannot do. A linked list wins when values are inserted and removed often, because only pointers change.
